generic_name: Etonogestrel and Ethinyl Estradiol Vaginal Ring
purpose: This medication is used to prevent pregnancy. It is a small, flexible ring that you place inside your vagina once a month. It is one of the most convenient forms of birth control available.
how_it_works: The ring slowly releases two hormones — estrogen and progestin — directly into your body. These hormones work together to stop your ovaries from releasing an egg each month. They also thicken the mucus in your cervix, making it harder for sperm to reach an egg.
common_side_effects: Some women experience headaches, nausea, breast tenderness, or mood changes when first using the ring. You might also notice some vaginal discharge, irritation, or discomfort. Spotting or light bleeding between periods can happen, especially in the first few months.
warnings: Do not use this ring if you smoke and are over 35 years old, as it increases your risk of serious blood clots, stroke, or heart attack. Tell your doctor if you have a history of blood clots, high blood pressure, migraines with aura, liver problems, or certain cancers. This ring does NOT protect against sexually transmitted infections (STIs).
typical_dosing: You insert one ring into your vagina and leave it in place for 3 weeks (21 days). Then you remove it and take a 1-week (7-day) break, during which you will likely get your period. After the break, you insert a new ring and repeat the cycle. The ring is changed once a month.
